fixes.explanation: That's the question, baker. They ask, "Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?" (Matthew 13:54). The text says they were astonished. I think they were saying it the way you'd say, "Hold on, who gave HIM the recipe?"
Not the fisherman, friend. The crowd asks, "Isn’t this the carpenter’s son?" (Matthew 13:55). Fisherman isn't in their question. I'd pack that answer away for another day.
Not the shepherd, baker. The hometown crowd asks, "Isn’t this the carpenter’s son?" (Matthew 13:55). They're pointing at what they know about His family. The word they use is carpenter.

False is right, baker. After the questions, the text says, "And they took offense at Him." (Matthew 13:57). So they're offended, not honoring Him. Jesus then says, "Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor."

It's the other way around, friend. Jesus says, "Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor." (Matthew 13:57). He names home, not strangers. Strangers and foreigners never come up in His line.

Right, baker. The text says, "And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief." (Matthew 13:58). Unbelief is the reason, and the verse says so plainly. I think that's a sad line, and I'd rather leave it just as the verse has it.

Noise isn't the reason, friend. The text says, "And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief." (Matthew 13:58). The verse gives unbelief as the reason. A noisy crowd never comes into it.
